hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/7e259eb428a1b2f16d2104452d48ea61.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x-\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-4}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x\right)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{5}{\pi}$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{5}{\pi}=2.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x\right)}$ to $\red{2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $2$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (two and one half, zero).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (two and one half, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, two) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (two and one half, zero).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x\right)}$ to $\blue{2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x-\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-4}$, which is equivalent to $2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}(x-2)\right)-4$, is a translation to the right by $2$ units and a translation downwards by $4$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(2,-2\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(4.5,-4)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at a maximum at (two, negative two) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (four and one half, negative four).

question.content:
**Graph $f(x)=2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}x-\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)-4$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
